decisions.note: Phase 1: no uniqueness guard on (user_id, bank_id, pattern_id) — pattern mappings follow the same insert-new-row + latest-active-by-updated_at semantics as digits mappings (LWW-friendly); only a non-unique index on (bank_id, pattern_id) for lookup speed.

Phase 1: relax account_card_mappings.last_digits to nullable in the unpublished 019/017 migrations (PostgreSQL DROP NOT NULL; SQLite table-rebuild), with a CHECK that at least one of last_digits/pattern_id is present; backend validator accepts 4-digit last_digits OR non-empty pattern_id. Chosen over sentinel value and separate table.

Phase 2: batch approval loop is continue-on-error — a mid-batch failure never rolls back approved items, the loop keeps going, failures are collected and reported in the result snackbar ('N aprobadas, M con error'); failed suggestions stay in the list for retry.

Phase 3: transaction provenance stored as a synced transactions.source column (proto field 21, PG migration 020, SQLite migration 018 + _version=18). Allowed values: 'manual' (default, incl. human-approved suggestions), 'auto_notification', future 'import_csv' (phase 5 dedup reuses it). Chosen over local-only marker: survives sync/reinstall and benefits phase 5.

Phase 5: monthly statement-import reminder implemented as a new STATEMENT_IMPORT event type in NotificationRepository's projection, driven by a device-local preference (marked account(s) + day of month) — integrates with the notification center, badge and the existing clean-slate OS scheduler. Chosen over a standalone one-off local notification (outside the idempotent scheduler pattern, invisible in the center) and over skipping the reminder.

Phase 6: background mechanism is the workmanager plugin (fluttercommunity, v0.9.x federated) — it already implements the native WorkManager + headless FlutterEngine pattern; rolling our own buys nothing for a periodic DB batch job. SQLite concurrency hardening is mandatory regardless of mechanism: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL (persists in the DB file, benefits the Kotlin NLS handle too) + per-connection busy_timeout on BOTH the Dart (DatabaseHelper) and Kotlin (NotificationDb.kt) sides, with short transactions in the background pipeline.

Phase 6: the background runner skips the LLM parser fallback (no ParserRemoteService in the headless composition root) — unmatched notifications stay pending and retry on next foreground processInbox. Avoids network + LLM quota burn in background, and sidesteps workmanager's Android 15 background-networking issue (#649).

Phase 6 session B: NO NLS-triggered one-shot enqueue in v1 — periodic 6h task only. Enqueuing from Kotlin would couple to the workmanager plugin's undocumented internal input-Data contract (dev.fluttercommunity.workmanager.BackgroundWorker) and could fire on a cold isolate before main() ever seeded parsers. Phase goal is eventual capture (hours), which the periodic task already meets. The seeding gap is closed anyway: the shared composition root will seed parsers from asset if missing, so the background isolate self-seeds.

Phase 6 session B: POST_NOTIFICATIONS (Android 13+) declared in the manifest and requested at app start inside NotificationSchedulerService.init() via AndroidFlutterLocalNotificationsPlugin.requestNotificationsPermission() — no permission_handler dependency. Also fixes the existing pocket_pilot_reminders notifications, which were silently undelivered on API 33+.
